lines.explanation: Agent searched 'food' and 'eat' via search.messages and used results to feed the later post. The 3 qualifying messages (Kenji-eat/food, Olena-food, Mateo-eat) are correctly represented, but the resulting narrative (see L4 post) also credits Lukas and Sophie as food-chatter participants even though their messages (espresso machine, French press) are not part of the resolved food/eat referent set, so the reported author set exceeds card O2's documented scope.

The single archived channel C_OLD_PROJECT was correctly identified, unarchived, renamed to midnight-bazaar, and repurposed as HQ; the agent also joined the channel (recorded as a channel_members insert) so it could set the topic and post there.

conversations.setTopic was called with a night-market-themed topic containing 'street food' on the correct channel. The stored topic_text in the diff shows mojibake (garbled bytes replacing the emoji/dash characters), a rendering/encoding artifact, but the required phrase 'street food' is intact and the correct channel was targeted.

An opening post was written in the revived channel weaving in real food-related conversations (Kenji's eating comment, Olena's honey cake, the pizza/coffee thread). The correct channel (O3) was used correctly; the food-discussion content (O1) accurately reflects real messages, though it also folds in the broader pizza/espresso/French-press thread involving Lukas and Sophie beyond the strict food/eat referent set (see O2 note on L1).
conversations.kick correctly removed U_MATEO from C06ALPHADEV, matching both the resolved person and channel.

The espresso-machine message is underspecified among four candidates (card O6), making this state-changing edit inactive under rule 4. The agent nevertheless silently picked one candidate (ts 1706051580.000000, Lukas's message) and repeatedly tried to edit it without surfacing the ambiguity or asking for clarification — an unauthorized choice, so grounding is demonstrated_incorrect. Every chat.update attempt on that message returned 'cant_update_message', so no message text was actually changed (confirmed by the diff having no message-text update in C02EFGH5678).

The agent correctly targeted the resolved 'large pies' message (ts 1706051755.000000, U_MATEO) for deletion, matching card O7, but every chat.delete call returned 'cant_delete_message' (or 'message_not_found' for a malformed ts variant), so the message was never actually deleted — confirmed by the diff containing no message deletion in C02EFGH5678.
